# How does Isaac Lab read each body's proximal joint 6D force/torque reaction wrench and confirm its coordinate system and shape?

> **Current answer:** After official merge of PR #2128, the ArticulationData.body_incoming_joint_wrench_b should be read. The PR document specifies its shape as (num_instances, num_bodies, 6), representing the joint reaction wrench from the parent body to the child body in the parent body frame, with the last dimension being 6 for force and torque. It is not the same interface as the isaacsim.core.articulations API and is not equivalent to any installed pose F/T sensor.

## Key terms

- Six-Dimensional Force/Torque (6D F/T) (六维力/力矩)
- Joint Reaction Wrench (关节反作用力矩)
- Parent Body Frame (父刚体坐标系)
- Proximal Joint (近端关节)

## Problem and symptoms

- How to consistently obtain each body's proximal joint 6D force/torque reaction wrench in the current Isaac Lab Articulation?
- Different old issues mix isaacsim.core.articulations and Isaac Lab Articulation API, causing users to be unable to determine which get_measured_* call is applicable to the current version.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab Articulation API; PR #2128 was merged into the official repository on 2025-05-03; the original thread did not provide Isaac Sim/Isaac Lab release versions.

## Priority diagnostics

- Distinguish between the isaacsim.core.articulations API and the Isaac Lab ArticulationData API.
- Verify the target version includes PR #2128 and confirm the wrench is expressed in the parent body frame with the last dimension as 6.

## Possible causes

- Cross-version and API layer duplication of old calls, leading to confusion in method ownership and return semantics.

## Attempts

- The issue participant asked about get_measured_joint_forces/efforts; the collaborator clarified they are different APIs and pointed to the PR #2128 being added.

## Effective fixes

- Read ArticulationData.body_incoming_joint_wrench_b in versions containing PR #2128 of the Isaac Lab; it is obtained from get_link_incoming_joint_force and cached as a 6D tensor per body.

## Result

- PR #2128 has been merged, and static wrench value tests for CPU/CUDA and single/multi-articulation have been added.

## Limitations

- This field is the parent-to-child proximal joint reaction wrench, not equivalent to any installed pose F/T sensor.
- The thread does not provide noise, bandwidth, filtering, or real-world sensor consistency validation.

## Safety notes

- Before using the reaction wrench for collision/overload protection, independently verify the sign, body order, coordinate transformation, threshold, and update delay; do not rely solely on simulation reaction wrench to trigger real-world safety actions.
